result.title: Auditing LLM Program Search for Bermudan Stopping with Primal--Dual Certificates
result.comment: Accepted at the MATH-AI Workshop at NeurIPS 2026
result.summary: LLM program-search agents are usually judged by the score that drives their search. We study LLM-driven search over Python exercise policies for Bermudan options, an optimal stopping problem where a trusted evaluator owns the simulation and a dual upper bound~$U$. For any policy, $0 \le V^\star - L_π\le U - L_π$; we report Monte Carlo estimates of both bounds with their sampling error. We audit 24 generation attempts from two pipelines, a six-pair feedback-representation ablation, and a holdout evaluated after selection was frozen. No selected generated program improves on Ridge LSMC consistently or by more than Monte Carlo uncertainty; holdout gap scores lie within $0.002$ of it. On six one-dimensional puts, a high-precision binomial reference places Ridge within Monte Carlo noise of optimal and attributes 99\% of the estimated gap to dual-bound looseness, so this dual audits validity but cannot certify progress at the search's scale. Structured memory showed no benefit over score-only memory in this ablation. Whether search ``worked'' depends on reporting rules: retaining the initial reference, freezing selection before holdout, and counting failures.

AI.brief_summary: 该工作审计 LLM 程序搜索生成的 Bermudan 期权行权策略，用原始—对偶界与蒙特卡洛误差给出带采样式误差的上下界，发现 24 次生成中没有程序能稳定或显著优于 Ridge LSMC，结构化记忆也不优于仅分数记忆，并指出搜索是否「成功」取决于报告规则。
AI.relevance_reason: 对偶上界可充当搜索停止与结果验证的信号，结构化记忆与纯分数记忆的对比涉及状态表示，可能为 LVR 的 STOP 决策、搜索验证与 latent 状态/记忆设计提供可核查线索，但领域与视觉多模态推理相距较远。
